scope: Static design and primary-source audit only; no implementation, native backward, resource measurement, admission, queue mutation, sync, or launch.
proposed_mechanism: Keep the two-way query referent logits and inference path unchanged.
Replace the PIRS scalar own-mask-IoU target with a detached identity-exclusivity target: q_positive * (1 - q_hardest_nonreferenced).
The intent is to assign high confidence only to hypotheses that overlap the referred object and avoid same-scene non-referred object masks.

rejection_reasons.finding: The proposal is a direct successor of the running PIRS mask-quality score target. The durable work record explicitly says not to create a PIRS-successor, renamed quality-score variant, or retuned target family.
The target is a hard-negative referent-ranking objective. Decision-aligned referent supervision was already rejected before design, including listwise, softmax-ranking, top-1, and renamed variants.

ConcreteNet already uses contrastive verbo-visual supervision to separate repeated same-class instances by pulling the referred instance and sentence together while contrasting remaining instances. The 2024 fine-grained-loss work already supervises each instance's spatial offset to the ground-truth referred object and states that cross-modal contrast improves instance separation. Changing the distance to mask overlap and placing it in the existing referent logits does not establish a new causal supervision unit.

The only new operation is a parameter-free multiplication or margin between known quantities inside an already prior-art score target. It does not add a new information path, new interaction between previously unconnected entities, or a distinct causal unit.

result: No admissible candidate remains in this batch. Keep the single open design slot empty rather than enqueueing a renamed PIRS/hard-negative-ranking successor.
